failures.triage_note: Our own JS validation gate and REST write path both fail to reject an empty title; confirmed via exact accessibility-tree ref (not a stale-query artifact) and confirmed server-side that the row was actually written with title='' after Save.
failures.expected: Per qa/runbooks/AGENT_SMOKE_RUNBOOK.md C.member.lightbox-edit-modal and qa/inventory/WHAT-TO-CHECK.md row 'Lightbox Edit-Media modal': 'save disabled while title empty' — clearing the Title field in the per-media Edit modal must disable the Save button so an empty title can never be persisted.
failures.actual: Cleared the Title field (confirmed value==='' on the exact input element) in the Edit Media modal for a freshly uploaded media item (media_id 125, slug smoke-free-upload-test). The Save button (class 'mvs-btn', in the Edit Media modal footer) remained enabled (disabled=false, no disabled attribute, no aria-disabled). Clicking Save succeeded (no client-side block, no visible validation error) and the REST write persisted: wp_mvs_media_index.title for media_id 125 became an empty string. This is a real data-loss bug, not just a UI gating miss — the backend also does not reject an empty title.
